findings.title: The named limit's parenthetical 'there' reads as pointing at schemas/**
findings.recommendation: The parenthetical after 'lowercase prose "openspec" outside `schemas/**`' opens with 'there the scan matches the product-name forms', whose nearest antecedent is `schemas/**` — the one place this change makes the scan match every case. Reword so the referent is unambiguous, e.g. '... outside `schemas/**` (outside `schemas/**` the scan matches only the product-name forms `OpenSpec`/`Openspec`; ...)' or move the qualifier into the parenthetical: '(in every file outside `schemas/**` the scan matches ...)'.

findings.title: The new schemas sentence carries a dangling appositive
findings.recommendation: 'In a file under `schemas/**`, every file the shipped-file walk returns there, `openspec` in ANY case is residue' interrupts the subject with an appositive that names the domain twice. Suggested: 'In every file the shipped-file walk returns under `schemas/**`, `openspec` in ANY case is residue, not only those two forms: ...'. The member table row already says 'for `openspec` in any case', so the meaning is not in doubt; this is wording only.

commentary: Probed hardest at the seams a widened residue rule usually breaks: whether the admitted list's substring/column matching survives a case-insensitive pattern (it does — positions and lengths are unchanged), whether any other spec or doc restates the scan as case-sensitive (none outside orbit-cli-name itself; orbit-user-docs' case-insensitive rule is a separate check over docs), whether the shipped-file walk and rc03b's pinned listing agree on the five schema files (they do), and whether a project-local fork would hide the fix in this very repo (there is none). The forked-schema named limit is honest; a user-level override under the global data dir would carry the same stale text for the same reason, but nothing creates one automatically, so it is not worth a sentence.

direction.reasoning:
The change is small, its premise reproduces on the live checkout, and every claim it makes about current state held when read.
`orbit instructions specs` still serves `openspec/specs/<capability>/` and `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`; a case-insensitive grep of `schemas/` finds exactly the four lines the proposal names (schema.yaml 17, 39, 55; templates/proposal.md 18); the resolver comments sit at lines 52 and 97 and `getProjectSchemasDir` returns `orbit/schemas`; all three files named for pin moves are pinned in rc03b-untouched-modules; this repo has no `orbit/schemas/` fork, so the package fix reaches its own propose flow.
The scan change is sound as designed: `admits` compares column and length, which `/openspec/gi` preserves, no admitted entry names a schema file, and the per-path switch in `occurrences` is the only edit the helper needs. Task 1.3 shows the widened oracle able to fail over the real package before the fix, and task 1.2's fixture pairs a failing schema line with a passing src literal, so both sides of the per-path choice are exercised.
The two remaining notes are spec wording; neither changes what an implementer would build. Go ahead to apply.
